candidates.tagline: Tesla's AI taxi drove on the wrong side of the road and dropped people off in intersections
candidates.story: Tesla's Cybercab launched in Austin in September 2026 as a no-steering-wheel autonomous taxi with dramatic butterfly doors, but its rocky first month brought passenger reports of driving on the wrong side of the road, phantom braking, drop-offs in intersections, butterfly doors closing improperly — and the NHTSA opened an investigation.
candidates.why_funny: Tesla promised a seamless autonomous future, then delivered a car that drives on the wrong side of the road and ejects passengers into intersections.
candidates.alt: A sleek white Tesla Cybercab autonomous robotaxi parked on a San Francisco street in June 2026, showing its minimalist exterior with no visible steering wheel or outside door handles

candidates.tagline: Apple's 2026 smart home hub design innovation: a 2002 computer they discontinued 22 years ago
candidates.story: Apple announced its long-awaited smart home hub for October 13, 2026, and the big design reveal is that it's a miniature version of the iMac G4 from 2002 — the same half-dome base, polished metal arm, and floating display that Apple used for a computer they stopped selling in 2004.
candidates.why_funny: After years of promising to reinvent the smart home, Apple's breakthrough was to dig up a design they buried during the George W. Bush administration.
candidates.alt: The Apple iMac G4 from 2002, with its iconic white half-dome base and flat-panel display floating on a polished metal arm — the same design Apple reportedly revived for its 2026 HomePad smart home hub
